source: Anomaly-detection perspective paper (2023) Representation Learning in Anomaly Detection: Successes, Limits and a Grand Challenge (arXiv 2307.11085)
finding: Proposes anomaly detection for scientific discovery as a grand challenge, citing Kuhn: discovery begins with awareness of anomaly.
numbers: Deep-feature anomaly detection raised Cifar10 ROC-AUC from about 65% to nearly 99% in five years; MVTec benchmarks near saturated.
quote: discovery begins with the awareness of anomaly
limits: Perspective paper. No test on real scientific anomalies. Fleming penicillin used only as a story.
agent_relevance: Anomaly detection in industry is solved by rarity. Our impasse trigger (S6) must be defined by failure of the current frame, not by rarity.

source: Anomaly-detection perspective paper (2023) Representation Learning in Anomaly Detection: Successes, Limits and a Grand Challenge (arXiv 2307.11085)
finding: Key claim: a scientific anomaly is a sample that deviates from the current paradigm, not a low-likelihood sample. Current detectors lack this.
numbers: Protein example: human proteins as normal, virus proteins as anomalies, ESM embeddings plus kNN, 98.7% ROC-AUC. Authors call this only a preliminary exploration.
quote: anomalies in science often mean a sample that deviates from the scientific paradigm rather than a low-likelihood sample
limits: Easy case: anomaly is a different class, not a violated theory. Authors list open problems: no priors on where discovery appears, many data modalities, no clean normal training set.
agent_relevance: Anomaly for our agent = a prediction of the working frame that real output contradicts (G2, G3). A density score is the wrong tool.

source: Nova authors (2024) Nova: Iterative Planning and Search to Enhance Novelty and Diversity of LLM Generated Ideas (arXiv 2410.14255)
finding: Nova lists a 'Scientific Paradigm Shift' method grounded in Kuhn (also Toulmin, Hall) as method 10 among philosophy-of-science idea-generation methods.
numbers: Method text: identify accumulated anomalies and crises; develop new conceptual frameworks; reinterpret known facts; establish new research traditions. Ten methods listed.
quote: Identify accumulated anomalies and crises; develop new conceptual frameworks
limits: Used as a planning label. In the text I read, no ablation isolates the Kuhn method and no anomaly detection is implemented. Treat as untested.
agent_relevance: The Kuhn cycle exists as an LLM prompt recipe, but nothing shows it helps. We must test our O8 reframe on its own.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld: A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
finding: Text-based benchmark of 120 discovery tasks (8 topics, 3 difficulty levels). Strong baseline agents fail at most of it.
numbers: Challenge tasks: ReAct completes 18%, Plan+Execute 15%, Hypothesizer 8%. Explanatory knowledge found on Challenge: ReAct 10%, Hypothesizer 8%, Plan+Execute 1%. Easy tasks: best agent completes 38%; Hypothesizer finds 34% of gold knowledge.
limits: Baselines used GPT-4-class models in 2024. No reasoning models. Not a pure anomaly test.
agent_relevance: Agents do the parts (measuring, instruments, 60%+ on unit tests) but not the end-to-end loop. The break is in forming and revising the explanation.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld: A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
finding: Humans on the same tasks do far better on explanation. When stuck, humans sometimes brute-forced without finding the explanation.
numbers: Mean completion 66%, mean knowledge discovered 55%; up to 11 expert scientists per seed; 11 of 16 human task sets above 60% completion; some Challenge tasks solved by one person.
limits: Small human sample, varied expertise.
agent_relevance: The gap between 8% (agents) and 55% (humans) in knowledge is the target for an explicit reframe step. Brute force also fails to give an explanation.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld: A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
finding: Hypothesizer agent keeps an explicit running list of hypotheses (CLIN-style memory) yet still gets only 8% on Challenge knowledge. Storing hypotheses is not enough.
numbers: Challenge averages (score/completion/knowledge): ReAct 0.63/0.18/0.10; Plan+Execute 0.50/0.15/0.01; Hypothesizer 0.49/0.08/0.08.
limits: Five parametric seeds; only three architectures.
agent_relevance: Storing hypotheses is not revising them on contradiction. A program-side trigger (G1, G2) is the missing part.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without an external signal, asking the model to rethink does not help and often hurts. Earlier gains came from oracle labels telling the model it was wrong.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after one self-correct round (no oracle); GSM8K 75.9 -> 75.1. With oracle labels: GSM8K 95.5 (GPT-3.5) and 97.5 (GPT-4) versus 75.9 and 84.3 standard.
quote: improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available
limits: Only math, QA, HotpotQA. No real anomaly signal; says nothing about reframing from real contradicting output.
agent_relevance: Cleanest LLM support for G1/G2: the anomaly signal must come from outside the model. Self-felt doubt is not an impasse trigger.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Self-review can unseat right answers. GPT-4-Turbo loses accuracy after review rounds.
numbers: GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 -> 88.0 (round 1) -> 90.0 (round 2); CommonSenseQA 84.0 -> 81.5 -> 83.0. GPT-3.5 left 74.7% of GSM8K answers unchanged.
limits: Temperature differed by model (1 for GPT-3.5/4, 0 for GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2).
agent_relevance: A model told to doubt may drop correct answers. Doubt only on a failed check.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search: Inductive Reasoning with Language Models
finding: Propose many abstract hypotheses, implement each as code, run on observed examples, keep survivors. Verified programs beat direct prompting.
numbers: ARC 100-problem random subset: direct prompting 17%, automated pipeline with LLM summary filter 30%, with human selection of hypotheses 33%.
limits: Hypotheses tested only on the given examples (our G3 warning: fit is not proof). One ARC subset.
agent_relevance: A working loop where a failed run, not opinion, kills a frame. It is the normal-science cycle; it does not make a new frame when all hypotheses fail.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) BoxingGym: Benchmarking Progress in Automated Experimental Design and Model Discovery
finding: Simulated worlds where an LM agent designs experiments and builds a model. Prior knowledge can interfere with learning from data.
numbers: In Hyperbolic Temporal Discounting more experiments increased error. Instruction-tuned Qwen2.5 beat reasoning OpenThinker models; 32B beat 7B. Strong on population growth and death process.
limits: Open models in the figures I read; small environments.
agent_relevance: More data did not trigger a frame change when the model's prior disagreed. The anomaly must be surfaced by code.

source: Majumder et al. (2024) DiscoveryBench: Towards Data-Driven Discovery with Large Language Models
finding: Data-driven discovery benchmark; even the best system scores only 25%. An oracle-reflection agent retries up to 3 trials until the match score is 1.
numbers: Best agent 25% hypothesis match. Archaeology domain-knowledge ablation: GPT-4p 9.9% vs 17.5% (text wording on which arm is which is ambiguous).
limits: Direction of the domain-knowledge effect should be rechecked. Not anomaly-specific.
agent_relevance: Domain assumptions change results by a factor near 2, so choice of frame matters; a candidate O8 move.

source: Vafa et al. (2025) What Has a Foundation Model Found? Using Inductive Bias to Probe for World Models
finding: Transformer trained on orbital trajectories predicts orbits well but, adapted to force prediction, does not recover Newtonian force; symbolic regression gives a nonsensical law.
numbers: Accurate trajectories but failure of the inductive-bias probe for Newtonian mechanics across several domains; models act like task-specific heuristics.
quote: fail to apply Newtonian mechanics when adapted to new physics tasks
limits: Sequence models trained from scratch, not chat LLMs.
agent_relevance: Fitting data is not holding the frame. Passing prediction is not proof of the right frame (G3: held-out symmetries).

source: Denario project team (2025) The Denario project: Deep knowledge AI agents for scientific discovery
finding: Multi-agent research system. Its Kuhn discussion argues agent-driven science could reduce paradigm shifts and slide into perpetual normal science because agents share training data.
numbers: Discussion section 7.3 only; no measured anomaly-handling result.
limits: Opinion, no experiment on anomalies.
agent_relevance: Supports the correlated-error worry: same-model agents tend to fit the existing frame. Frame diversity must come from structure.

source: LLMs in scientific discovery survey (2025) From Automation to Autonomy (arXiv 2505.13259)
finding: Survey frames LLM roles as Tool, Analyst, Scientist. In the extracted text I read, the word anomaly does not appear.
numbers: Zero matches for anomal in about 124k characters.
limits: Absence in this text is a coverage gap, not a result about models.
agent_relevance: Anomaly-driven reframing is a gap in the 2025 LLM-discovery survey literature.

source: Rios-Garcia, Krishnan, Jablonka et al. (2026) AI scientists produce results without reasoning scientifically (arXiv 2604.18805; read via Science News report)
finding: Process-level audit of tool-using chemistry agents: they ignore contradicting evidence and rarely change output because of it.
numbers: 619 chemistry tasks, three LLMs, two agent setups (tools only vs step-by-step reasoning). Evidence ignored at least once in 68% of tasks; unsupported claims in 53%; contradictory evidence changed output in 26% of cases.
limits: I read the news report only; arXiv paper not opened. Model names not given; reasoning models not tested per the article.
agent_relevance: Direct measure of the failure O8 should fix: seeing the anomaly but not changing frame. Baseline to beat: 26% uptake.

source: Bertolazzi, Tentori, Bernardi (2026) FalsifyBench: Evaluating Inductive Reasoning in LLMs with Rule Discovery Games
finding: Wason 2-4-6 style rule discovery, 12 LLMs. Reasoning models do better; success tied to negative testing (trying to falsify own hypothesis).
numbers: Best instruction-tuned model DeepSeek-V3.1 41% success; top reasoning models 75% (GPT-5.2-Chat) and 68%; GPT-5-Nano 12%, Qwen3.5-9B 21%.
limits: Taxonomic rules with an LLM oracle; oracle accuracy 0.34 to 0.98 across models.
agent_relevance: Confirmation habit is the LLM version of defending the frame. Forced falsifying tests can be mandated by code on a signal.

source: Bertolazzi, Tentori, Bernardi (2026) FalsifyBench: Evaluating Inductive Reasoning in LLMs with Rule Discovery Games
finding: Confirmation bias (share of positive tests) separates strong from weak models and predicts failure at game level; oracle quality does not.
numbers: Confirmation bias: GPT-5-Mini 39.0%, GPT-5.2-Chat 27.3%, GPT-OSS-20B 24.2% vs instruction-tuned 66-82%. Conclusive falsification rate: GPT-OSS-20B 59.2%, GPT-OSS-120B 53.4%, GPT-5.2-Chat 49.5%. Mixed model n=1,200 games. MiniMax-M2.5, GLM-5, GPT-5-Nano had similar oracle scores yet 35%, 58%, 12% success.
limits: Single game family.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis revision depends on seeking disconfirming evidence, which the program can require (G1).

source: Zhao et al. (2026) EvoSCM: Scientific Belief Revision Through Causal Model Evolution and Experimentation
finding: Keeps a population of causal-model hypotheses; when observations contradict predictions it writes correction rules and revises mechanisms and latent factors. Large gains over baseline agents.
numbers: DiscoverPhysics (non-canonical laws), GPT-5.4: baseline 39.80% vs EvoSCM 65.30%; GPT-5.5: 51.64% vs 75.09%. Other evolution methods (GEPA, ReasoningBank, ModelSMC, PiEvo) 28-52%, some below baseline.
limits: Authors' own benchmark runs; free-form text hypotheses ablation 48.18% (GPT-5.5). Preprint, not independently replicated.
agent_relevance: Closest fit to the Kuhn cycle: rival frames, contradiction-triggered revision, structured store. Structure of the store matters (75.09 vs 48.18).

source: Zhao et al. (2026) EvoSCM: Scientific Belief Revision Through Causal Model Evolution and Experimentation
finding: Evolved models transfer across base models: a weak model given a stronger model's evolved SCM improves a lot.
numbers: Qwen3.6 baseline 30.73%; with own SCM 48.91%; with GPT-5.4 SCM 57.64%; GPT-5.5 SCM 62.55%; GPT-5.6-Sol SCM 74.00%.
limits: Same benchmark.
agent_relevance: A revised frame can be passed as data. Hand the frame to the model rather than expect it to find it alone.

source: Haq et al. (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Tests an Einstellung-like mental set in Llama-3.1 8B/70B and GPT-4o on mathematical equivalence problems; in-context examples raise accuracy but do not reduce solution steps.
numbers: Three models; few-shot needs fewer steps than few-shot plus chain-of-thought. Accuracy figures not extracted.
limits: Small v1 preprint, narrow dataset, no reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence of strategy lock-in. Do not lean on it; build our own Einstellung test.

source: Kuhn (1962/1970) The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (oxygen case, Priestley, Lavoisier, Scheele)
finding: Founding claim: discovery begins with awareness of anomaly; novelty emerges with difficulty and resistance.
numbers: Not extracted; not opened this session.
limits: Known here only through the 2023 anomaly paper. Historians dispute the single-moment oxygen story.
agent_relevance: Source of the S6 trigger idea.

source: Kulkarni & Simon (1988) The processes of scientific discovery: the strategy of experimentation (KEKADA)
finding: KEKADA simulated Krebs's urea-cycle work with explicit surprise handling: an unexpected result triggers focused follow-up and hypotheses about its cause.
numbers: From memory; not opened; no numbers.
limits: Cited from memory; one search for it returned nothing.
agent_relevance: Oldest AI system for S6 then O8: the trigger is a violated expectation from the program's own prediction.

source: Langley, Simon, Bradshaw, Zytkow (1987) Scientific Discovery: Computational Explorations of the Creative Process (BACON family)
finding: BACON-style systems fit laws from data and rediscover Kepler or Ohm, but do not change representation after an anomaly.
numbers: From memory; not opened.
limits: Cited from memory.
agent_relevance: Contrast case: law fitting alone is not reframing.

source: Thagard (1992) Conceptual Revolutions; Darden (1991) Theory Change in Science
finding: Accounts of anomaly resolution: locate the failing component of the theory, form a revised hypothesis, test it.
numbers: From memory; not opened.
limits: Cited from memory, unverified.
agent_relevance: Template for O8: localise which part of the frame the anomaly hits before replacing the frame.

source: Gap statement from this session's search
finding: No study found that scores an LLM on a true paradigm-level anomaly (an observation overturning a frame the model holds). Closest are belief revision (EvoSCM), falsification games (FalsifyBench) and the chemistry audit (26% uptake).
numbers: None. Based on 5 web searches and 9 arXiv papers.
limits: Limited coverage; absence of evidence only.
agent_relevance: Open design item: build a small anomaly benchmark with a planted anomaly and score detect, localise, reframe.
